subject: Request: regional SLA mitigation & one-time credit for Equinox (Deal DL-2026-1147)
messages:
From: Michael Nguyen <mnguyen@equinox.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.patel@equinox.ai, procurement@equinox.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional SLO concerns for pilot - request for temporary amendment

Karthik —

Thanks again for the quick kickoff last week. As we ramp the West Coast pilot into production we’re seeing sustained tail latency spikes during regional maintenance windows in the vendor region you recommended. Our infra team ran a quick impact analysis and expects a small window (2–3 weeks) where the 99.9% latency SLO for the dedicated model route will be missed during nightly rolling updates.

Two asks from Equinox:
- Can Redwood accept a temporary relaxation of the latency SLO for the West region (US-W) from 99.9% => 99.5% for a maximum of 21 days while we finish instance migration?
- If we incur any downtime/latency impact beyond that window, can we cap remedies to a one-time service credit not to exceed 10% of monthly committed spend for the pilot month?

We’ve attached the impact spreadsheet and can share more telemetry if needed. Please let us know what approvals are required — we’d like to lock this in before the next maintenance cycle (Thursday).

Best,
Michael Nguyen
Head of Platform, Equinox AI

Attachment: equinox-slo-impact-analysis.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Michael Nguyen <mnguyen@equinox.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SLO concerns for pilot - request for temporary amendment

Michael — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I’ve looped in Marissa and Jonas from deal desk/legal to scope what we can sign off on quickly. High level: Redwood is open to a time-boxed SLO relaxation and a capped remedy, but we typically require an amendment and some guardrails to avoid open-ended exposures.

Marissa / Jonas — can you review the attached and advise what form of amendment (short-form SLA addendum vs. contract exhibit) is fastest? Also flag any concerns with the 21-day window and 10% cap.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SLO concerns for pilot - request for temporary amendment

Thanks Karthik — reviewed Equinox’s impact analysis. Notes:
- We can do a time-limited SLO tolerance (99.9 -> 99.5) for up to 21 calendar days, documented as a short addendum (Proposed Amendment EQ-1147).
- The 10% one-time credit cap is within precedent for pilot ARR sizes, but we need Exec clearance to make it binding without a longer-term contractual concession.
- Require an operational rollback clause: if the issue extends beyond 21 days, Redwood will revert to standard SLOs and remedies apply per the base contract unless Equinox agrees to a renewal or dedicated-reservation that compensates the exposure.

I’ve drafted a two-paragraph amendment and attached as PDF. It includes: time window, affected region, capped credit, measurement window, and rollback language.

Attachments: proposed-amendment-EQ-1147.pdf

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec approval required: temporary SLO tolerance + capped credit for Equinox (DL-2026-1147)

Lauren — requesting executive signoff for a non-standard, time-boxed SLO amendment for Equinox (deal DL-2026-1147). Summary below: 
- Customer: Equinox AI (pilot)
- Ask: US-W latency SLO from 99.9% -> 99.5% for maximum 21 days; one-time remedy cap = 10% of monthly committed spend for the pilot month.
- Proposed concessions in exchange: a) formal amendment limited to the migration window, b) operational rollback triggers, c) 12-month minimum committed term if Equinox requests further exceptions.
- Attachments: impact analysis, proposed amendment PDF; HubSpot deal link included.

Can you confirm whether to approve the one-time concession and allow signing the short-form amendment? If approved, we will issue the amendment and coordinate countersignature + billing hold for the credit cap.

Jonas Weber
Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval required: temporary SLO tolerance + capped credit for Equinox (DL-2026-1147)

Jonas / Team — approved.

Decision rationale (summary):
- The exposure is limited (21 days) and operational risk is mitigated by rollback triggers.
- 10% one-time credit cap is acceptable for the pilot ARR and aligns with precedent; not approving would risk losing the pilot to a competitor.
- Require that the amendment includes an explicit expiry date and a clause that any extension requires a separate commercial review.

Action items:
1) Jonas — send the short-form amendment to Equinox with a 48-hour turnaround request for countersignature. Attach the impact workbook.
2) Marissa — add the rollback trigger language and the explicit expiry date to the PDF and send to Jonas.
3) Karthik — inform the customer that exec signoff is granted and share next steps (DocuSign + billing note).

Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
